model.author: Bio3D Project
model.modifications: Anatomical GLB with 4 chambers, auricles, aortic arch with 3 branches, pulmonary trunk, superior/inferior vena cava, pulmonary veins, and surface coronary arteries.

short.en: Upper right chamber that receives oxygen-poor blood returning from the body via the vena cava.

detail.en: Receives deoxygenated blood from the superior vena cava, inferior vena cava, and coronary sinus, then pushes it through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle. Houses the SA node.

short.en: Upper left chamber that receives fresh oxygen-rich blood arriving from the lungs.

detail.en: Receives oxygenated blood through four pulmonary veins from the left and right lungs and passes it through the bicuspid (mitral) valve into the left ventricle.

short.en: Lower right chamber that pumps oxygen-poor blood up through the pulmonary artery to the lungs.

detail.en: Has a thinner muscular wall than the left ventricle because it pumps blood at lower pressure across the short pulmonary circuit to the lungs.

short.en: Lower left chamber — the strongest chamber, forming the heart's apex and pumping blood to the whole body.

detail.en: Possesses the thickest myocardium (~3× thicker than the right ventricle) to generate high systemic pressure (~120 mmHg) driving blood through the aorta to every organ.

short.en: The body's largest artery — arches upward from the left ventricle to carry oxygen-rich blood to all organs.

detail.en: Elastic artery arising from the left ventricle. Its arch gives off three major branches (brachiocephalic, left common carotid, left subclavian) supplying the head and arms before descending.

short.en: Two large blue veins (superior and inferior) bringing used, oxygen-poor blood back into the right atrium.

detail.en: The superior vena cava drains blood from the head, neck, and arms; the inferior vena cava drains the abdomen and legs. Listed separately in NEET mode.

short.en: Branches left and right to carry oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle to both lungs.

detail.en: The only artery in the adult body carrying deoxygenated blood. Arises as the pulmonary trunk from the right ventricle and bifurcates beneath the aortic arch.

short.en: Four vessels at the back that bring fresh, oxygen-rich blood from the lungs into the left atrium.

detail.en: The only veins in the adult body carrying oxygenated blood (two from the left lung, two from the right lung, entering the posterior left atrium).

short.en: Blood vessels hugging the outside of the heart muscle to feed the heart itself with oxygen.

detail.en: Branch directly from the base of the aorta (above the aortic semilunar valve) to supply oxygenated blood to the myocardium. Blockage of these vessels causes myocardial infarction (heart attack).

short.en: Large upper vein draining deoxygenated blood from the head, neck, and upper limbs.

detail.en: Formed by the union of the left and right brachiocephalic veins; enters the superior aspect of the right atrium without a valve.

short.en: Large lower vein returning deoxygenated blood from the abdomen, pelvis, and legs.

detail.en: Ascends through the diaphragm to enter the inferior posterior part of the right atrium, guarded by a rudimentary Eustachian valve.

question.en: Tap the strongest chamber that forms the heart's apex and pumps blood to the whole body.

explanation.en: The left ventricle has the thickest muscular wall because it pumps oxygen-rich blood through the aorta to the entire body.

question.en: Which blood vessel is the largest artery carrying oxygenated blood out of the heart?

explanation.en: The aorta rises from the left ventricle, arches upward, and branches to supply oxygen-rich blood to every organ.

question.en: Tap the blood vessels on the outer surface of the heart that supply oxygen to the heart muscle itself.

explanation.en: The coronary arteries wrap around the heart's exterior to nourish the hard-working heart muscle (myocardium).

question.en: Tap the blue branching vessel that sends oxygen-poor blood to the lungs.

explanation.en: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs to pick up oxygen.

question.en: From where do the coronary arteries arise to supply the myocardium?

explanation.en: Left and right coronary arteries branch directly from the aortic sinuses at the base of the ascending aorta.
